metadata.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure

problem_summary.summary: Support adding lowercase words and searching patterns where each dot matches exactly one lowercase letter.
problem_summary.input_output: Implement WordDictionary(), addWord(word), and search(word). Add has no return value; search reports whether any stored word matches the whole pattern.
constraints: Added words use lowercase English letters
Search patterns use lowercase English letters and '.'
At most two dots occur in any search pattern
At most 10,000 addWord and search calls

brute_force.explanation: Store words in a list. For a search, test only equal-length words, comparing each position unless the pattern character is a dot. Return as soon as one full match is found.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A pattern matches a word exactly when their lengths agree and every non-dot position contains the same character. Checking every stored word covers all possible matches.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(L) per add; O(WL) worst case per search across W stored words of maximum length L.

optimized.explanation: Store words in a 26-way trie. Search follows one child for a letter; at a dot, recursively try each existing child. A match succeeds only when the pattern ends at a terminal node.
optimized.correctness_idea: Each trie edge represents one exact next letter. Trying every child at a dot explores all and only the allowed letter choices, and the terminal check enforces a complete stored word of the same length.
optimized.time_complexity: O(L) per add; O(26^D * L) worst case per search, where D is the number of dots (at most 2) and L is pattern length. Exact-letter branches add no branching.
optimized.space_complexity: O(T) for trie nodes, where T is the total number of distinct prefix nodes; search recursion uses O(L) stack space.

steps.condition: Each word shares suffix path a -> d but has a different first edge.
steps.action: Mark b-a-d, d-a-d, and m-a-d terminal.

steps.condition: The root has no p child.
steps.action: Return false without exploring deeper nodes.

steps.condition: The dot tries each root child; each then follows a -> d to a terminal.
steps.action: Return true on the first matching branch.

steps.condition: The literal b selects one branch; the two dots traverse its a then d path.
steps.action: The path ends at terminal bad, so return true.

edge_cases.handling: The trie follows one exact path and checks its terminal marker.
That branch returns false while other existing children are still tested.

edge_cases.case: Pattern length differs from a stored word
edge_cases.handling: The traversal ends at a nonterminal node or missing path, so no match is reported.

edge_cases.case: Pattern ends at a nonterminal prefix
edge_cases.handling: The final check returns false; a longer stored word is not an exact match.
